text: 你看什么、信什么，就会被塑造成什么样，且自己根本意识不到。
en: What you watch and what you believe shapes what you become, without you realising it at all.

text: 你只会觉得：我所见为真，我所想是对。
en: You only feel: what I see is true, what I think is right.

text: 你会发现，现在网上不管出个什么事，只要稍微有点争议，评论区立马变为两个阵营。
en: You will find that now, no matter what happens online, as long as it is slightly controversial, the comments section immediately becomes two camps.

text: 一边是这么说的，一边是那么说的，两边都觉得自己占着理，都觉得对面那帮人不是蠢就是坏。
en: One side says this, the other side says that; both sides feel they are in the right, and feel the people on the other side are either stupid or bad.

text: 并且，这两边用的所谓“事实”都不是一回事。
en: Moreover, the so-called 'facts' used by both sides are not the same thing at all.

text: 比方说，同样一件事，A看到的是一套截图、一段视频、一个分析。
en: For example, for the same matter, A sees one set of screenshots, one video, one analysis.

text: B看到的则是另一套截图、另一段视频、另一个分析。
en: B sees another set of screenshots, another video, another analysis.

text: 两边人拿到的所谓“证据”完全是反的，那你让他们怎么聊？
en: The so-called 'evidence' obtained by both sides is completely opposite — so how do you expect them to talk?

text: 聊不到一起去。
en: They cannot talk together.

text: 更可怕的是：两边都觉得自己是那个掌握了真相的人。
en: Even more terrifying: both sides feel they are the ones who grasp the truth.

text: 我原来也觉得，只要我多看、多听、多查，我就能离真相近一点。
en: I used to think that as long as I read more, listened more, and checked more, I could get closer to the truth.

text: 后来我发现我太天真了，现在的问题并非是你查得够不够多，是你查到的那些东西，本身就是被人筛过一遍的。
en: Later I discovered I was too naive. The problem now is not whether you check enough; it is that the things you find have themselves been filtered by others.

text: 你打开手机，刷出来的每一条，背后都站着一堆人，他们的工作就是研究你，研究你喜欢看什么、讨厌看什么、会对什么生气、会对什么感动。
en: You open your phone, and behind every item you scroll to stands a bunch of people whose job is to study you — studying what you like to watch, what you dislike, what makes you angry, what moves you.

text: 然后他们就把这些内容喂到你嘴边，一条一条，一天一天。
en: Then they feed this content to your mouth, one by one, day by day.

text: 时间长了，你看见的世界，就是他们想让你看见的世界。
en: Over time, the world you see is the world they want you to see.

text: 你以为你在做选择，其实你只是在几个预设好的选项里头挑一个相对顺眼的。
en: You think you are making choices, but in fact you are only picking a relatively pleasing one among several preset options.

text: 这话题聊到这里，你可能觉得我是在骂那些做平台的、做算法的。
en: Talking about this topic here, you may think I am scolding those who run platforms and make algorithms.

text: 并不是的，其实人家也只是干活挣钱罢了。
en: Not at all. Actually, they are just working to earn money.

text: 我真正想要表达的是：我们自己在这里边，到底起到了多大的作用？
en: What I really want to express is: how big a role do we ourselves play in this?

text: 我们老说“信息茧房”，老觉得是别人把我们关起来了。
en: We keep saying 'information cocoons', always feeling others have locked us up.

text: 但其实，我们自己也在拼命往里头添砖加瓦。
en: But in fact, we ourselves are desperately adding bricks and tiles to it.

text: 我们只选我们爱看的，只信我们想信的，只跟聊得来的人待着。
en: We only choose what we love to watch, only believe what we want to believe, and only stay with people we get along with.

text: 谁要是跟我们想的不一样，我们就不搭理他，或者骂他。
en: Whoever thinks differently from us, we ignore him, or scold him.

text: 这不就是自己把自己关进去了吗？
en: Isn't this locking ourselves in?

text: 而且这里头最悲哀的一点是：你关得越久，就越出不来。
en: And the saddest point here is: the longer you stay locked in, the harder it is to get out.

text: 因为你已经不习惯外面的空气了，你看见不同意见，第一反应不会是好奇“他为什么这么想”，只会反感“他怎么这么想”。
en: Because you are no longer used to the air outside. When you see different opinions, your first reaction is not curiosity — 'why does he think this way' — but only disgust — 'how can he think this way'.

text: 你失去了那种对未知的好奇，对不同的宽容。
en: You have lost that curiosity about the unknown, and tolerance for differences.

text: 你把自己活成了一个闭环，进来的都是你认得的，出去的都是你不待见的。
en: You have lived yourself into a closed loop: what comes in is all what you recognise, what goes out is all what you dislike.

text: 我经常在想，我们现在这么容易生气，这么容易站队，这么容易把别人当敌人，是不是也跟这有关系？
en: I often wonder: are we now so easily angered, so easily taking sides, so easily treating others as enemies — is it also related to this?

text: 因为你每天看到的，都是那些被挑出来刺激你的东西。
en: Because what you see every day are things picked out to stimulate you.

text: 你看不到对方的难处，看不到事情的复杂，看不到这世上大多数人都只是在挣扎着过自己的日子。
en: You cannot see the other party's difficulties, cannot see the complexity of matters, cannot see that most people in this world are just struggling to live their own lives.

text: 你看到的，是一个被简化过的、非黑即白的世界：好人是全好，坏人是全坏。
en: What you see is a simplified, black-and-white world: good people are entirely good, bad people are entirely bad.

text: 对的事是绝对的对，错的事是彻底的错。
en: Right things are absolutely right, wrong things are thoroughly wrong.

text: 但真实的生活不是这样的。
en: But real life is not like this.

text: 真实的生活是：好人也会干混蛋事，坏人也有心疼的人。
en: Real life is: good people also do bastard things, and bad people also have people they care about.

text: 你以为对的事，换个人看可能就是错的。
en: What you think is right may be wrong in someone else's eyes.

text: 你恨得牙痒痒的人，也有他的理由和苦衷。
en: The people you hate to the point of gritted teeth also have their reasons and difficulties.

text: 这事我到现在也还没完全整明白，但一点我比以前清楚了，就是别那么急着下结论，别那么急着把跟自己不一样的人推出去。
en: I still haven't fully figured this out, but one thing is clearer to me than before: don't rush to conclusions, and don't rush to push away people different from yourself.

text: 你可以不认同他，但你得知道他为什么那么想。
en: You may disagree with him, but you must know why he thinks that way.

text: 因为知道了，你才能真的说清楚你为什么不同意。
en: Because only by knowing can you really explain clearly why you disagree.

text: 不然你骂半天，骂的都是你自己脑子里想象出来的那种靶子。
en: Otherwise, after scolding for a long time, what you scold are targets imagined in your own mind.

text: 还有一点，就是别太相信自己的“独立思考”。
en: Another point: don't trust your own 'independent thinking' too much.

text: 这话可能不太好听，但我越来越觉得，所谓的独立思考，很多时候就是个幻觉。
en: This may not sound pleasant, but I increasingly feel that so-called independent thinking is often an illusion.

text: 你想的那些东西，往前倒几层，全是别人喂给你的。
en: The things you think, traced back a few layers, are all fed to you by others.

text: 你以为是你自己想出来的，其实是你刷多了、听多了，自然就长在脑子里了。
en: You think you came up with them yourself, but in fact, after scrolling and listening a lot, they naturally grew in your brain.

text: 真正能称得上独立思考的，是你能把自己的想法拆开来看：这个想法哪里来的？
en: What can truly be called independent thinking is being able to take your own ideas apart and look at them: where did this idea come from?

text: 我为什么信它？
en: Why do I believe it?

text: 有没有可能我信错了？
en: Is it possible I believe wrongly?

text: 如果错了，我愿不愿意改？
en: If wrong, am I willing to change?

text: 能做到这一点的人，说实话，不多。
en: People who can do this, honestly, are not many.

text: 包括我自己，也经常做不到。
en: Including myself — I often cannot do it either.

text: 但知道了，起码会在自己又开始上头的时候，愣上一楞，扪心自问上一句：这是我自己想的，还是别人想让我这么想的？
en: But knowing it, at least when I start getting worked up again, I pause for a moment and ask myself: is this my own thought, or is it what others want me to think?

text: 既然没人能看见全貌，那你就得时刻提醒自己，你看见的只是一部分。
en: Since no one can see the whole picture, you must constantly remind yourself that what you see is only a part.

text: 你的那部分，不假，但也不全。
en: Your part is not false, but neither is it complete.

text: 你信的那些东西，可能有一部分是真的，但也有一部分，是你想让它真的。
en: The things you believe may partly be true, but partly, they are what you want to be true.

text: 你讨厌的那些人，可能有一部分是坏的，但也有一部分，是你把他们想坏的。
en: The people you hate may partly be bad, but partly, they are what you imagine to be bad.

text: 你得给自己留个心眼，留个口子。
en: You must leave yourself a watchful eye, leave an opening.

text: 这个口子，是用来装那些你不爱听、不想听、甚至一听就烦的东西的。
en: This opening is for holding things you don't like to hear, don't want to hear, and even feel annoyed as soon as you hear them.

text: 这事难就难在这里，因为往这个口子里装东西，太难受了。
en: The difficulty lies precisely here, because putting things into this opening is very uncomfortable.

text: 比方说，要你去看一个你讨厌的人的文章，你会气得想摔手机。
en: For example, asking you to read an article by someone you hate will make you so angry you want to smash your phone.

text: 要你去了解一个你反对的观点，你会觉得脑子极其混乱。
en: Asking you to understand a view you oppose will make your brain feel extremely confused.

text: 要你去跟一个跟你三观完全不同的人聊天，你恨不得扭头就走。
en: Asking you to chat with someone whose values are completely different from yours will make you want to turn around and leave.

text: 但你得忍住。
en: But you must endure it.

text: 因为只有在这些让你难受的时刻，你的脑子才是在转的。
en: Because only in these moments that make you uncomfortable is your brain actually turning.

text: 只有在这些让你不舒服的瞬间，你才是在长进。
en: Only in these uncomfortable moments are you actually growing.

text: 你天天舒舒服服地待在自己那一亩三分地里，听人说你爱听的话，信你愿意信的理，那你十年之后，还是今天的你。
en: If you comfortably stay in your own little patch every day, listening to people say what you love to hear, believing reasons you are willing to believe, then ten years later, you will still be today's you.

text: 不，你比今天还糟，因为你的壳更硬了，更听不进人话了。
en: No — you will be worse than today, because your shell is harder, and you listen to people even less.

text: 我这些年最大的一个体会就是：当你发现自己跟谁都能聊两句，不再急着反驳人，不再觉得自己天下第一对的时候，你是真的变强了。
en: My biggest realisation over these years is: when you find you can chat with anyone, no longer rush to refute people, and no longer feel you are the most right in the world, you have truly become stronger.

text: 并非是那种咋咋呼呼的强，是那种心里有底的强。
en: Not that loud, blustering kind of strength, but the kind of strength with a solid foundation in your heart.

text: 你知道这世界复杂，你知道自己有限，但你也不慌。
en: You know this world is complex, you know you are limited, but you are not panicked.

text: 因为你能看懂别人为啥那么想，你能理解那些跟你不一样的人，也有他们的道理。
en: Because you can understand why others think that way, and you can understand that people different from you also have their reasons.

text: 这种感觉，比你天天刷手机刷出来的那种“我对了”的快感，要踏实得多。
en: This feeling is much more solid than the 'I'm right' pleasure you get from scrolling your phone every day.

text: 人这一辈子，其实就是在跟自己脑子里那点东西较劲。
en: A person's life is actually spent wrestling with the things in one's own mind.

text: 你装进去什么，你就信什么。
en: Whatever you put in, you believe.

text: 你信什么，你就活成什么样。
en: Whatever you believe, you live as.

text: 你若是只装那些顺溜的、舒服的、哄你开心的东西，那你活到最后，就是一场自欺欺人的梦。
en: If you only put in smooth, comfortable things that coax you into happiness, then living to the end, you live a self-deceiving dream.

text: 梦醒了，啥也没剩下。
en: When the dream wakes, nothing is left.

text: 你若是愿意往里装点硌得慌的、难嚼的、让你难受的东西，那你活的这一辈子，至少是真真切切地跟这个世界撞过，疼过，也懂过。
en: If you are willing to put in things that are jarring, hard to chew, and make you uncomfortable, then this life you live has at least truly collided with this world, hurt, and understood.
